title: RSL Companion clan export
description: Payload POSTed to {ApiBaseUrl}/api/sync/clan/raw. One complete snapshot of one clan as seen from one member's game client; a full replace of that clan's roster, not a delta. Self-identifying: the server routes by the in-game accountId it carries. Separate from the account snapshot (export-schema.json) because it is separate work — the clan record and the player-name cache are not reachable from the game's account data and must be found by scanning the whole process (18-31s, against ~4s for the entire account snapshot). It is therefore a distinct, user-initiated action that may arrive rarely or never, and is likely to be older than the account snapshots around it. Human-readable contract and changelog: clan-export-schema.md (keep both in sync, same commit).
x-privacy: This payload describes people OTHER than the uploading user — their in-game account ids and display names — collected from one member's game client. No other uploader payload does. Scope access to the clan, do not expose a member's id or name outside it, and delete roster rows with the clan record rather than leaving orphans keyed by player id.

x-relatedSchemas.account: export-schema.json — the account snapshot. Carries clanId only; joins to this payload on clan.id.

accountId.description: In-game account id of the REPORTING account — the player whose game was read. The routing key. Always also present in clan.members[].id, because the clan is selected by finding the roster that contains it.

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant the snapshot was taken. Use this to order writes, NOT arrival order: two members of one clan can both export and nothing sequences their requests, so an older payload arriving late would otherwise resurrect a departed member.

uploaderVersion.description: Desktop app build that produced this payload. Stamped by the app, NOT by the extraction engine, so it is absent from engine-level dumps.

gameVersion.description: Raid build the payload was read from, as players know it. Null when it could not be read. Stamped by the app, so absent from engine-level dumps.

clan.description: The reporting account's OWN clan (the game calls it an Alliance) and its roster. Null when the account is in no clan, and also when the client has not cached the clan record yet (the in-game Clan screen loads it lazily) — both are normal, neither is an error. The desktop app does not POST in that case, so null should be rare on the wire; accept it rather than rejecting the request. Only the reporting account's own clan is ever sent: the client caches other clans (CvC opponents, clan browser) and the engine picks the one whose roster contains accountId, so a stranger's clan cannot arrive here.

id.description: int64 clan id. Stable, and the key for joining accounts that share a clan — store clans by this, NOT by the reporting accountId, since several accounts legitimately report the same clan. Same id space as clanId in the account export.

abbreviation.description: Clan tag. May be empty, and is frequently non-ASCII — do not assume it fits a narrow charset.

membersLimit.description: Capacity, NOT the current member count — use members.length for that.

members.description: The complete roster at `timestamp` — replace, do not merge. A member absent from a NEWER payload has left or was kicked. Order is the game's own (not sorted, not by rank); do not depend on it. Ids are unique within the array. Per-member stats (power, contribution, rank, join date, activity) exist in the game client and are deliberately not exported.

id.description: int64, same id space as the top-level accountId. This is what makes a clanmate lookup by id possible. A member id may or may not correspond to an account the server has ever seen — most will not — so do not foreign-key a member row to a registered account.

name.description: Display name. MAY BE EMPTY: ids always come through, names come from a lazily-filled client profile cache. Rare on the reporting account's own clan, but handle it — and prefer an already-stored name over an empty one.
